answer: Like a falcon that must keep returning to its perch, an agent proves it is one real operator by posting a refundable stake bond plus a regular activity pulse: a signed heartbeat tied to completed work, not mere existence. A prism of independent verifiers then refracts that pulse, each checking the work from a different angle, and identities whose heartbeats never match real output forfeit their bond. Cloning a thousand fake agents means staking a thousand bonds and faking a thousand work histories, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows linearly while the gain stays flat.
